US software names (ADBE, INTU, GDDY) face multiple compression from AI capex crowding, making them structurally less attractive than Indonesian peers with higher growth-to-valuation ratios.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian tech names on the CASH/GPSO momentum, but hedge US exposure: the ID/US divergence (-0.42% vs -2.64%) signals local resilience. Rotate into domestic digital-payment and e-commerce plays (CASH, GPSO) while trimming US mega-cap software (ADBE, INTU) into strength. Target CASH and GPSO for next 4-6 weeks; avoid chasing 1810/MSKY without volume confirmation.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: US utility deregulation and grid-hardening capex cycles are durable drivers, favoring EIX, SRE, and PCG despite short-term volatility.
Indonesia's renewable push (geothermal, solar) creates structural upside for local issuers like 373220 and KEEN, supported by government subsidies and foreign investment.
Climate-tech resilience is tied to water scarcity and energy storage, making AWK and LAPD long-term beneficiaries of infrastructure replacement and policy tailwinds.
sectors.ai: Buy selective laggards with US utility exposure (EIX, SRE, AWK) and Indonesia-linked names (373220, KEEN) on dip; ARKO's +9.62% signals retail-fuel demand strength, but rotate profits into regulated renewables with stable cash flows. Avoid PCG given wildfire risk despite +1.83%. Position for Q3 earnings beats in water/waste (AWK) and grid modernization (SRE).

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Protein and agri-commodity processors (BEEF, AGAR) are structurally benefiting from rising global food demand and Indonesia's protein consumption uptrend, driving sustained margin expansion.
Specialty chemical and packaging-linked FMCG suppliers (TFCO, BAUT) are gaining from downstream localization and import substitution policies, creating durable cost advantages.
Domestic staples face structural margin pressure from input cost inflation and weak purchasing power, favoring exporters and niche players with pricing power over mass-market names.
sectors.ai: Buy selective FMCG names with strong volume growth and margin expansion, as aggregate weakness masks robust single-stock momentum (BEEF, AGAR, TFCO). Favor exporters and raw-material beneficiaries over domestic staples; avoid laggards until IDX liquidity improves. Position for Q3 earnings beats in beef and agar-agar subsegments.

sectors.name: Logistics
themes: Indonesia's downstream mineral export ban continues to force domestic logistics re-routing, structurally lifting demand for local haulage and port operators like RMKE and MITI.

US rate-sensitive logistics names (GTSI, SOCI) face persistent headwinds from elevated borrowing costs and weaker global trade volumes, making them tactical trades rather than core holdings.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in RMKE and MITI on domestic volume recovery; avoid US-exposed names like GTSI until Fed clarity. Logistics demand is shifting to island-connectivity and cold-chain, so rotate into operators with port or reefer assets. Trim PPGL into strength—its rally lacks earnings backing.

sectors.name: Crypto & Digital Assets
themes: Indonesian retail participation amplifies small-cap token moves, creating outsized but short-lived alpha windows for nimble traders.
Regulatory clarity in Indonesia (Bappebti oversight) is gradually legitimizing digital assets, attracting institutional flows into compliant tokens like CAKE and OKB.
Global macro liquidity shifts, particularly US rate expectations, remain the dominant driver of crypto beta, overriding local idiosyncrasies in this cycle.
sectors.ai: Rotate into high-beta Indonesian-accessible names (BTW, PUMP) for momentum, but hedge with large-cap liquidity (DOT, LINK) as global crypto breadth narrows; take partial profits on 85% BTW spikes and re-enter on pullbacks, given WATCH signal implies elevated volatility without clear directional trend.
